summary: A provider that its driver stopped, because the driver could no longer serve it, now ends with the reason driver-stopped on its harness record. Before, that record looked like the provider's own exit (#4743). The seat's end reason then reads "its harness exited: driver-stopped" instead of "crashed on signal 15".

schema.detail: No schema change. The harness record's optional reason field already exists, and harness.observed already carries it.

rules.detail: Two consumers read the reason. (1) A seat's end reason is kind harness-exited with diagnostic driver-stopped, where it was crashed (with the signal) or completed. (2) A resume whose provider the driver stopped before it bound its native session fails as resume-exited, saying the driver stopped it, not as harness-refused.

compatibility.detail: Mixed-version fleets with the previous release interoperate. The reason is an optional field every build already reads and carries. A previous-release daemon shows the same end reason, harness-exited with diagnostic driver-stopped. Its resume verification fails such a resume as harness-refused, naming driver-stopped in the text. Nothing else branches on the reason.

recovery.detail: Rolling back stops writing the reason. Records already written keep it, and an earlier build reads them as described above.
